title: Server-Sent Events (SSE) with TypedResults.ServerSentEvents
description: Implement real-time server-to-client streaming using the new TypedResults.ServerSentEvents helper in ASP.NET Core 10.

data.text: Server-Sent Events (SSE) is a standard that allows a server to push real-time updates to a client over a single long-lived HTTP connection. Unlike WebSockets, SSE is unidirectional — the server sends messages, and the client receives them as an event stream. SSE works over standard HTTP, making it easier to integrate with existing infrastructure like proxies and CDNs.

.NET 10 introduces TypedResults.ServerSentEvents<T>, a strongly-typed helper that sets the correct Content-Type (text/event-stream), manages the connection lifecycle, and streams data as SSE messages. You can use it in both Minimal APIs and controller-based endpoints.

data.text: On the client side, use the EventSource API to connect to the SSE endpoint. Each message is received as a message event with the data field containing the serialized payload.

data.text: In controller-based APIs, return TypedResults.ServerSentEvents<T> or IResult with a yielded sequence. The framework handles setting the response headers and streaming the data.

data.title: When to Use SSE vs WebSockets
items: Use SSE when the server only needs to push data to the client (unidirectional).
Use WebSockets when both client and server need to send messages (bidirectional).
SSE works through standard HTTP proxies and CDNs without special configuration.
SSE reconnects automatically on transient network failures.

data.title: Summary
points: TypedResults.ServerSentEvents<T> provides a strongly-typed SSE response in .NET 10.
Use IAsyncEnumerable<T> to yield data continuously.
Set the Content-Type to text/event-stream for controller-based endpoints.
SSE is ideal for notifications, live feeds, and progress updates.
data.takeaway: TypedResults.ServerSentEvents makes implementing real-time streaming in ASP.NET Core 10 straightforward and type-safe, with first-class support in both Minimal APIs and controllers.
